title.en: Directional derivative on a quadratic surface

summary: Rotate a direction on a height field and compare the measured slope with the gradient dot product.
objective: Build a quadratic surface with a draggable sample point, a rotating unit direction and a linked slope readout.
intent_signals: Build a quadratic surface with a draggable sample point, a rotating unit direction and a linked slope readout.
Rotate a direction on a height field and compare the measured slope with the gradient dot product.
example_prompts: Build a quadratic surface with a draggable sample point, a rotating unit direction and a linked slope readout.
Create an explorable 3D explanation of directional derivative with level curves and readout.
negative_signals: Not a general optimizer or particle force model.
not_for: Not a general optimizer or particle force model.

entities.name: Height mesh
entities.guidance: Sample the rectangular domain into a regular indexed mesh; preserve a visible zero plane and equal x/y scale.

entities.name: Direction and tangent
entities.guidance: Draw u in the domain plane and a lifted tangent segment with vertical change D_u f; do not label the lifted 3D vector as the 2D gradient.

entities.name: Level curves and readout
entities.guidance: Add selected-height contours, signed slope value and an angle dial; use length and labels as well as color.

state_contract.model: Use f(x,y)=x*x+2*y*y on [-2,2]^2; grad f=(2*x,4*y), u=(cos(a),sin(a)), D_u f=grad f dot u. Coordinates are mathematical units.
state_contract.authority: The selected domain point and direction angle determine surface point, analytic gradient and directional derivative; camera orbit changes none of them.
actions: Drag the sample point within the domain.
Rotate the unit direction without changing its norm.
Toggle finite-difference comparison with a positive step that stays inside the domain.
Reset point, angle and comparison step.

invariants: At the origin grad f is zero; no unique steepest direction is displayed.
Opposite unit directions give opposite signed slopes.
A direction perpendicular to a nonzero gradient has zero directional derivative.
motion_guidance: Animate only the direction dial or a deliberately parameterized point path; derive all arrows from current analytic values.
Keep arrow display gain explicit and compare finite differences only as approximations.
known_limits: Not a general optimizer or particle force model.
A finite triangulation approximates the smooth surface; its face normals do not replace the analytic derivative.
Curated recipe only; no runtime scene or rendered behavior has been verified for this record.

claims.statement: For a differentiable scalar function, the directional derivative along a unit vector equals its gradient dotted with that vector.
claims.scope: Differentiability and a unit domain direction; the chosen quadratic is an authored example.

object_craft.structure: Sample the rectangular domain into a regular indexed mesh; preserve a visible zero plane and equal x/y scale.
object_craft.material: Matte surface with restrained height palette; opaque arrows and contour strokes retain signs without relying on specular lighting.
